capabilities: Sync a whole vault peer-to-peer between devices over WebRTC with no server
Co-edit notes live with named cursors, avatars and CRDT merging
Invite friends with a code or link and approve or block joining devices
Keep per-note version history locally and preview or restore versions
Keep conflicting note versions as separate private copies
extras: README urges backing up the vault before use, states there has been no independent security review, and notes it has only been tested with up to 3 devices (mesh is meant for about 5). Sync only happens when devices are online at the same time; a TURN server is optional for strict networks.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to share a vault live with other people for collaborative editing without a paid sync service or a self-hosted server.

relations.evidence: Each note is a shared document (Yjs, a CRDT).
Built on Yjs, y-codemirror.next, Trystero and diff-match-patch.

summary: Peer-to-peer plugin that shares a whole vault live with friends over WebRTC, with Google-Docs-style co-editing and named cursors, no server or account.
